# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 12
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 12

---

*[THE PATTERN REPEATS. Tertia. The final arrest. Thomas blesses his people.]*

1. There was another woman — Tertia, wife of Misdaeus, the king's own son. She heard about Thomas and she came to him.

2. She heard him. She believed. She was baptized.

3. She also left her husband's bed.

4. Misdaeus went to his father and told him what Thomas had done.

5. The king's rage was beyond what it had been before. He sent soldiers to arrest Thomas.

6. When they took Thomas, his believers wept. Many of them were shaking with fear.

7. Thomas looked at them. "Don't cry," he said. "My Lord is powerful. He can do anything. And he will bring out from prison everyone who belongs to him."

8. They brought him before the king.

9. The king said: "What have you done to my son? What have you done to Charisius?"

10. Thomas said: "I have done them no harm. I told them about the living God. I told them about eternal life."

11. "And in doing that," the king said, "you have torn my kingdom apart."

12. Thomas said: "I didn't cause the trouble. The truth causes trouble in the hearts of those who love darkness."

13. "Then stop teaching it," the king said. "Stop leading my people off the edge."

14. "Truth cannot be condemned by those who refuse to receive it," Thomas said.

15. The king had nothing left to say to that. He ordered Thomas back to prison and said he would decide the matter later.

16. Thomas walked to the prison praising God.

17. Believers followed him there — all the way to the prison gate — and he taught them.

18. Mygdonia was among them. Thomas spoke to her specifically, giving her the last instructions she would need.

19. He turned to all of them. "Brothers and sisters," he said. "Hold to the faith. My Lord Jesus Christ is with you. He will not abandon anyone who believes in him."

20. He put his hands on them and blessed them. Then he turned and went inside.

---
*PNEUMA note: Thomas's exchange with the king (vv.9–14) is a masterclass in compressed apology. Each charge is met with a reframing: not harm but proclamation; not discord but truth's natural opposition; not condemnation but reception. Thomas's final act before entering prison — blessing each person individually — is rendered with the weight of a farewell.*
